key_insight: BASOC reduces optimal-control problems by balancing state variability with value-function sensitivity along locally optimal trajectories.
engineering_relevance: The framework targets reduced-order models and surrogate feedback controllers for high-dimensional nonlinear systems, including aerospace flow control.
method: Use trajectory optimization and Pontryagin’s minimum principle to collect state and co-state data.
Construct and balance state and value-gradient covariance matrices.
Form an oblique projection to approximate the value function and support reduced-order control.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports demonstrations on a nonlinear three-dimensional system where POD and balanced truncation perform poorly, and on the nonlinear complex Ginzburg–Landau equation; it also establishes an equivalence to initial-condition balancing for linear-quadratic control.
watch_item: Because the projection is learned from locally optimal trajectories, its reliability outside the sampled state regimes requires validation.
paper_title: Balanced Active Subspaces for Optimal Control via Trajectory Optimization
